# AI Development Workflow Configuration
#
# This file declares which workflow integrations this repository uses.
# Keep it declarative and repo-safe: select providers here, but do not store
# secrets, tokens, hostnames, or other environment-specific credentials.
#
# Repository mode fields (`mode`, `workflow_hub.product_repos[]`, and
# `product_repo.workflow_hub`) are documented in
# docs/workflow/development-workflow/repository-modes.md. Omit `mode` to keep
# the default `single_repo` behavior.
#
# Product release contracts are optional non-secret metadata under either
# `workflow_hub.product_repos[].release` or `product_repo.release`. Supported
# fields are:
#
#   release:
#     base: main                         # optional; defaults to default_branch
#     branch_pattern: release/v{version} # optional; may use {version} and {product_repo}
#     changelog_owner: product_repo      # product_repo|hub|current_repo|hub_reference|not_applicable
#     tag_owner: product_repo
#     github_release_owner: product_repo
#     deployment_evidence_owner: product_repo
#     cleanup_evidence_owner: product_repo
#     tracker_reconciliation_owner: hub
#
# Never store local checkout paths, credentials, token values, secret names,
# secret values, or environment-specific account details in the versioned
# release contract. Use `.ai-dev-workflow.local.yaml` for machine-local values.
#
# See docs/workflow/development-workflow/README.md and
# docs/workflow/development-workflow/integrations/ for integration-specific setup.
#
# Important:
# - review.on_draft.runner is consumed by the Step 7a internal review gate
#   protocol (91-orchestrate-work-protocol.md).
# - review.on_draft.github and review.on_ready.github are consumed by
#   scripts/development-workflow/pr-review-loop.sh for external automated PR
#   review (Step 7).
# - Other sections are advisory until additional scripts or agents adopt them.
#
# Behavior for automated PR review:
# - If this file is absent, or both review.on_draft.github and
#   review.on_ready.github are omitted or empty, the review loop reports skipped
#   (not configured).
# <!-- TEMPLATE-OWNED-END -->

schema_version: 2

review:
  on_draft:
    # Ordered list of internal reviewers for draft PRs (Step 7a).
    # Supported values:
    #   claude        — local-runtime reviewer.
    #   cursor        — local-runtime reviewer.
    #   codex         — local-runtime reviewer.
    #   dsh           — local-runtime reviewer.
    #   coderabbit    — hosted-service reviewer.
    #   codex-github  — hosted-service reviewer.
    runner:
      - claude

    # Ordered list of GitHub/App/CLI reviewers that can safely evaluate draft
    # PRs. These run before the PR is converted to ready.
    # Supported today by pr-review-loop.sh: greptile, devin, coderabbit,
    # coderabbit-cli, local-ai-reviewer, pr-agent, codex-github,
    # claude-code-action, haystack, copilot, bugbot, ronda.
    github:
      - pr-agent

  on_ready:
    # Ordered list of GitHub/App/CLI reviewers that run only after draft gates
    # are clean and the PR has been converted with `gh pr ready`.
    # local-ai-reviewer is the ready-phase reviewer for this repository
    # (PR-Agent covers the draft phase). codex-github and bugbot are
    # intentionally not listed here; restore either in this list to re-enable
    # a hosted ready-phase reviewer.
    github:
      - local-ai-reviewer

  # Optional: TWO independent reviewer-loop cycle caps enforced by
  # pr-review-loop.sh (issue #1502; dual-cap decision recorded on PR #1507's
  # review). Neither cap resets on a HEAD SHA change alone (see the comment
  # above reviewer_loop_history_entries_count in pr-review-loop.sh for why:
  # a reset-on-push design would make both caps dead code for the exact
  # motivating failure, PR #1492's 18-cycle loop, where nearly every cycle
  # produced a new commit).
  #
  # max_cycles (PER-RUN cap, default 10): resets to 0 at each orchestration-
  # run boundary. Conforms to Protocol 91:1719 verbatim ("Initialize cycle
  # = 0 once per orchestration run ... escalate when the run reaches
  # max_cycles"). The "run boundary" is whatever the caller's
  # PR_REVIEW_LOOP_RUN_ID env var identifies — see pr-review-loop.sh's usage
  # doc for RUN_ID / PR_REVIEW_LOOP_RUN_ID. When the caller does not set a
  # stable run id, every invocation is its own isolated run, and this cap
  # effectively never trips on its own (the lifetime ceiling below still
  # protects in that case). Escalates with REASON=max_cycles_exceeded.
  # PR_REVIEW_LOOP_MAX_CYCLES env var overrides this value.
  #
  # max_total_cycles (LIFETIME ceiling, default 25): never resets, counts
  # across the PR's entire review-loop lifetime regardless of run
  # boundaries. This is the structural backstop that does not depend on
  # every caller correctly threading a stable run id through every
  # invocation — a per-run-only cap would leave total effort unbounded for
  # a PR resumed across many separate orchestration runs, which is exactly
  # the "runs until someone notices" failure #1502 exists to end. Escalates
  # with the distinct REASON=max_total_cycles_exceeded, checked only after
  # the per-run cap does not fire, so an operator can tell "one run ran
  # away" (max_cycles_exceeded) apart from "many runs cumulatively ran
  # away" (max_total_cycles_exceeded). PR_REVIEW_LOOP_MAX_TOTAL_CYCLES env
  # var overrides this value.
  #
  # Uncomment to override the defaults:
  # max_cycles: 10
  # max_total_cycles: 25
  #
  # Optional: per-platform reviewer wait budgets in whole seconds (1-999999;
  # issue #1789). Each platform waits for its own budget; a wait that runs out
  # with no verdict and no failure evidence is reported as waiting_on_reviewer
  # / reviewer-no-verdict-yet, not as a failure. Resolution order: the
  # one-run --max-wait override, then this block (CODEX_GITHUB_MAX_WAIT wins
  # over the codex-github key), then the built-in defaults (bugbot 2400,
  # codex-github 1800, every other platform 1200; Devin only is shortened on
  # spec/* and implementation-plan/* branches). An invalid value warns and
  # falls back to the default; a claude-code-action value above 3600 does too.
  # See "Reviewer wait budgets and outcome classes" in
  # docs/workflow/development-workflow/protocols/93-automated-reviewer-loop-protocol.md.
  # Uncomment to override:
  # wait_budgets:
  #   bugbot: 2700
  #   local-ai-reviewer: 1500
  #
  # Bugbot is the default ready-phase GitHub reviewer for this repository.
  # CodeRabbit remains supported as an opt-in reviewer (`coderabbit` for the
  # GitHub App, `coderabbit-cli` for the local CLI), but it is not a default
  # gate because vendor rate limits/spending caps can block otherwise-clean PRs.
  #
  # CodeRabbit CLI platform options (local CLI reviewer; place "coderabbit-cli"
  # in on_draft.github or on_ready.github to opt in; independent from the
  # "coderabbit" GitHub App platform):
  #   rate_limit_policy: warn      # warn|strict; default warn
  #
  # Local AI reviewer platform options (local-only CLI reviewer; enabled first
  # in on_draft.github by default before PR-Agent and ready-phase reviewers):
  #   LOCAL_AI_REVIEWER_COMMAND        — optional override; when unset,
  #                                      local-ai-reviewer.sh defaults from
  #                                      LOCAL_AI_REVIEWER_BACKEND
  #   LOCAL_AI_REVIEWER_BACKEND         — codex (default) or http (alias: openai_compat)
  #   LOCAL_AI_REVIEWER_DISABLE_DEFAULT=1 — do not apply a bundled preset default
  #   LOCAL_CODEX_REVIEWER_BIN         — Codex binary for the bundled preset (default: codex)
  #   LOCAL_CODEX_REVIEWER_MODEL       — optional model for the bundled Codex preset
  #   LOCAL_AI_REVIEWER_MODEL           — model id for http
  #                                      (example: deepseek-v4-pro)
  #   LOCAL_AI_REVIEWER_API_BASE_URL   — Chat Completions API base URL for http
  #                                      (example: https://api.deepseek.com;
  #                                      falls back to OPENAI_BASE_URL when unset)
  #   LOCAL_AI_REVIEWER_API_KEY         — API key for http (or DEEPSEEK_API_KEY /
  #                                      OPENAI_API_KEY / LOCAL_AI_REVIEWER_API_KEY_COMMAND)
  #   LOCAL_AI_REVIEWER_TIMEOUT        — default local command timeout (default: 300)
  #   LOCAL_AI_REVIEWER_GRAPH_STRATEGY — none|auto|code-review-graph|graphify
  #   LOCAL_AI_REVIEWER_DISABLED=1     — intentionally skip with
  #                                      REASON=disabled_by_config
  #                                      (or override on_draft.github locally)
  #
  # Configurable codex-github options (set via env vars or script flags to pr-review-loop.sh / codex-github-reviewer.sh):
  #   Setup/verification guide: docs/workflow/development-workflow/integrations/codex-github.md
  #   CODEX_GITHUB_TRIGGER_PHRASE  — trigger phrase sent to the bot (default: "@codex review")
  #   CODEX_GITHUB_BOT_LOGIN       — GitHub login of the Codex bot account
  #                                  (default: "chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]"; verify from GitHub App settings)
  #   CODEX_GITHUB_POLL_INTERVAL   — default polling interval for codex-github via pr-review-loop.sh (default: 60)
  #   CODEX_GITHUB_MAX_WAIT        — default maximum wait for codex-github via pr-review-loop.sh (default: 1800)
  #   CODEX_GITHUB_PRE_TRIGGER_WAIT — wait for existing current-head Codex evidence before posting a trigger; 0 disables (default: 60)
  #
  # Additional options available as script flags to codex-github-reviewer.sh (passed via pr-review-loop.sh):
  #   --poll-interval <seconds>    — polling interval while waiting for bot response
  #   --max-wait      <seconds>    — maximum total wait time for bot response
  #   --pre-trigger-wait <seconds> — wait for existing current-head evidence before posting a trigger; 0 disables
  #
  # Copilot platform options:
  #   Prerequisites: an active GitHub Copilot seat or the Copilot for Pull Requests feature
  #                  must be enabled on the repository. GitHub Enterprise Server (GHES) is
  #                  not supported. See docs/workflow/development-workflow/integrations/copilot.md
  #   COPILOT_BOT_LOGIN  — override the default Copilot bot login
  #                        (default: "copilot-pull-request-reviewer[bot]")
  #
  # Bugbot platform options (Cursor Bugbot — requires the Cursor GitHub App installed
  # on the repository; place "bugbot" in on_draft.github or on_ready.github):
  #   BUGBOT_BOT_LOGIN        — override the Bugbot bot login
  #                             (default: "cursor[bot]")
  #   BUGBOT_CHECK_NAME       — override the check-run name to poll
  #                             (default: "Cursor Bugbot")
  #   BUGBOT_TRIGGER_COMMENT  — override the trigger comment posted to start a run
  #                             (default: "bugbot run")
  #
  # Ronda platform options (GitHub-facing reviewer bot; place "ronda" in
  # on_draft.github or on_ready.github). Ronda reacts to the PR automatically
  # (no trigger comment) and posts a pull-request review plus a single check
  # run per head SHA, created exactly once, already completed:
  #   RONDA_BOT_LOGIN   — override the Ronda bot login
  #                       (default: "ronda[bot]")
  #   RONDA_CHECK_NAME  — override the check-run name to poll
  #                       (default: "Ronda review")

  # Each supported runner's own reviewer is reachable by construction. Other
  # entries are probed against this machine at each gate run. A machine that
  # intentionally lacks runtimes may narrow the list locally to avoid a
  # reduced-coverage warning:
  #   review:
  #     on_draft:
  #       runner:
  #         - cursor
  # The local file takes precedence over this file for the local environment.
  # See docs/workflow/development-workflow/protocols/91-orchestrate-work-protocol.md
  # Step 7a for the full multi-reviewer gate procedure.

  # Optional: policy for unavailable configured internal reviewers.
  # Protocol 91 Step 7a enforces this policy at runtime.
  #
  # Allowed values:
  #   warn                    — (default) Emit a warning comment on the PR and proceed with
  #                             the reachable subset. Hard-fails only if zero reviewers are reachable.
  #   fail-if-any-unavailable — Hard-fail the Step 7a gate whenever any listed reviewer is
  #                             unreachable, even if others are reachable.
  #
  # Uncomment and set to override the default:
  # internal_reviewers_unavailable_policy: warn

issue_tracker:
  # Supported examples: linear, github_projects, github_issues, jira, clickup, notion, none
  provider: github_projects
  # GitHub Projects project number (the integer in the project URL, e.g. /users/<owner>/projects/1).
  # Used by workflow-lib.sh as a fallback when GITHUB_PROJECT_NUMBER env var is not set.
  # Required for tracker status updates (update_tracker_status_best_effort) and status reads
  # (get_tracker_status_for_issue) to function without setting an environment variable.
  project_number: 1
  # custom_fields: flat key-value map of provider-specific fields.
  # Each integration doc defines which keys are recognised and their effect.
  # Unrecognised keys are silently ignored by scripts that do not consume them.
  # Read individual values with: workflow_issue_tracker_custom_field <key>
  # (defined in scripts/development-workflow/workflow-lib.sh)
  #
  # Example (Linear):
  #   custom_fields:
  #     project: my-linear-project-id
  # Example (GitHub Projects board whose classification field is not named Type):
  #   custom_fields:
  #     type_field: Custom Type
  #
  # custom_fields:
  #   project: ""

vcs:
  # Supported examples: github, gitlab, bitbucket, other
  provider: github

browser_automation:
  # Supported examples: cursor_ide_browser_mcp, playwright_mcp, playwright_cli, none
  provider: playwright_cli

template:
  # Set to true when this repository IS a framework template (i.e., it ships workflow
  # tooling to be consumed by downstream projects). When true, Protocol 02 Step 0
  # (Template-Fit Check) is mandatory before writing any implementation plan.
  # Leave false or omit for downstream consumer repositories.
  is_template: true

  # Optional: upstream template repository reference (owner/repo format for GitHub).
  # When set, the retrospective protocol (Step 3b) cross-references each finding
  # against the specified template repository's issue tracker. Leave empty or omit to skip.
  # Note: this is set by DOWNSTREAM repos pointing back to their template origin —
  # the template repo itself leaves this empty.
  repository: ""

  # Optional: the template version last applied by the sync-template skill.
  # Written automatically by sync-template after a successful sync.
  # Used by the retrospective cross-reference step to identify "already fixed upstream" findings.
  last_synced_version: ""

  # Optional batch provenance; per-path bases live in .ai-dev-workflow.sync-state.json.
  # Never use this SHA to fill declined/unknown entries in an existing ledger.
  last_synced_commit: ""

# guardrails — declares how much authority AI agents have when advancing work through the
# development workflow. This section is OPTIONAL. When omitted, all values resolve to the
# documented safe defaults below, preserving today's conservative, human-reviewed behavior
# (agents do not merge pull requests and do not start backlog work without confirmation).
#
# Enforced at runtime by Protocols 90, 91, and 95 via three-layer precedence:
# repo config (this file) → session overrides → invocation overrides (highest priority).
#
# See docs/workflow/development-workflow/guardrails.md for plain-language explanations,
# mode descriptions, worked examples, stop conditions, and audit requirements.
# See docs/workflow/development-workflow/guardrails-enforcement.md for the runtime
# enforcement reference (effective-guardrails resolution, five enforcement gates,
# named stop conditions, audit-evidence rules).
#
# Two-step lifecycle (default for this template):
# Delegated execution permits Backlog starts and merges within the per-stage
# risk limits below. Bounded prelude still reports the resolved policy before
# mutation — see docs/workflow/development-workflow/bounded-run-prelude.md.

guardrails:
  # mode: delegated — agents may merge within per-stage permissions and risk limits.
  mode: delegated

  # backlog_start — agents may start eligible Backlog work without an additional
  # policy confirmation.
  backlog_start:
    allow_without_confirmation: true

  # stages — delegated merge authority is enabled up to medium risk.
  stages:
    spec:
      may_open_pr: true
      may_merge_pr: true
      max_merge_risk: medium
    plan:
      may_open_pr: true
      may_merge_pr: true
      max_merge_risk: medium
    implementation:
      may_open_pr: true
      may_merge_pr: true
      max_merge_risk: medium

  # stop_conditions — baseline stops that hold in all modes (additive, never removable).
  stop_conditions:
    - unclear_requirements
    - architecture_decision
    - failing_ci
    - unresolved_blocking_review
    - high_risk_change
    - destructive_action
    - missing_tracker_context
    - missing_required_secret_or_permission
    - push_verification_failed

  audit:
    pr_disposition_record: required
    work_item_ledger_record: required

  # Optional project-owned categories; no rules are enabled by this example.
  # Highest matching rule wins; sensitive/tooling High floors cannot be lowered.
  # See docs/workflow/development-workflow/guardrails.md (Project Path Risk Maps).
  # risk_paths:
  #   - glob: "docs/store/**"
  #     risk: medium
  #     reason: "Store review package documentation"

# No-target GitHub Projects scan reserve; whole numbers 0..5000 only.
# Invalid/empty values warn and fall back to 1000 (Protocol 90 Step 1a).
portfolio_scan:
  graphql_reserve: 1000

# Merge-session heuristic headroom; quota is observed, never reserved.
merge_budget:
  graphql_reserve: 1000
